column3: “Again and again” renders rising early and speaking.
“Again and again” renders rising early and sending.
“The prophets” identifies the speakers; “forever and ever” compresses from antiquity to perpetuity.
“Whom I will bring” narrows the plural “them” to Nebuchadnezzar; contempt renders hissing.
Bride and bridegroom are named in reverse order.
The purpose phrase is moved before the names; “contempt” renders hissing.
“Coastlands” renders a singular island or coast.
“Their hair” supplies the reference of the cut corners.
The repetition of “all the kings” before each country is compressed.
“One after another” renders each to his brother.
“Never ... again” makes the negated rising explicit.
